confirmed.title: Five label-map keywords can never match the shipped label file (short-form labels); bucket/tub/barrel/file/cab are silently unmapped
confirmed.scenario: assets/models/imagenet_labels.json is the short-form ImageNetLabels.txt. Its entries are "tub", "bucket", "barrel", "file" and "cab". The rules use the long-form phrases 'tub, vat' (line 26), 'barrel, cask' (line 27), 'cab, hack' (line 30), 'file, file cabinet' (line 34) and 'bucket, pail' (line 41). The word-boundary regex for 'bucket, pail' cannot match the text "bucket", so these five classes always return null from hitForLabel. The unit checks in scripts/ai-test.ts pass because they feed long-form labels ('electric fan, blower', 'ashcan, trash can, ...'), not the shipped ones. On the phone, the objects that signal plumbing or tank work in an Indian home are a bucket or tub under a tap and a blue water drum (ImageNet 'barrel'). They carry most of the probability mass and route nowhere, so a tap photo lands on 'could not tell' or a weak guess. The user reported switchboard, appliances and carpentry as recognised, but not the tap.
confirmed.fix:
**Keyword changes in `C:\dk\mobile\src\ai\labelMap.ts`**
- Line 26: change `'tub, vat'` to `'tub'`. The word-boundary regex keeps it from matching "bathtub", which has its own keyword.
- Line 27: change `'barrel, cask'` to `'barrel'`. This also covers "rain barrel", so that keyword becomes redundant but harmless.
- Line 30: change `'cab, hack'` to `'cab'`. "cabbage butterfly" is excluded by the word boundary.
- Line 34: change `'file, file cabinet'` to `'file'`. It is the only label containing that word.
- Line 41: change `'bucket, pail'` to `'bucket'`. For tap shots, move it into the plumbing `tap_leak` rule on line 26 instead of leaving it under cleaning. A bucket under a tap is the common rural scene, and broom, mop and swab still cover cleaning.

**Test in `C:\dk\mobile\scripts\ai-test.ts`**
- Load `../assets/models/imagenet_labels.json` and assert that specific shipped labels route as intended:
  - 'tub' to plumbing
  - 'bucket' to plumbing
  - 'barrel' to plumbing/tank_overflow
  - 'file' to carpentry
  - 'cab' to mechanic
  - 'electric fan' to appliance/fan_dead
  - 'switch' to electrical/switchboard
  - 'washbasin' to plumbing
- Do not use the reviewer's proposed assertion that every keyword matches at least one real label. It would fail on deliberate synonym keywords kept for long-form label files; 'sink', for example, has no entry in the shipped file.

confirmed.title: Android BACK while the diagnosis sheet is up closes the app instead of returning to the camera
confirmed.scenario: /home is the only entry in the stack (index.tsx uses router.replace('/home') or <Redirect>), and Lens registers no BackHandler (there is none anywhere in src). The sheet is a full-screen paper page that looks exactly like a pushed screen, so a judge who snaps a fan, reads 'Looks like ...' and presses the hardware back button / back gesture to go back to the camera instead sees the whole app vanish to the launcher - it reads as a crash. confirmed.title: Camera-first home has no 'Your active job' entry (and no change-role link): a job in progress is invisible from the Lens
confirmed.scenario: CustomerHome runs openJobId() on focus and shows the 'Your active job / Open job' notice ('Coming back to the home screen must never lose a job in progress'), plus <ChangeRoleLink/>. Lens, which is now the default customer home, renders neither. Two-phone check: customer snaps, requests a worker, lands on /job/[id]; then closes and reopens the app (normal while waiting), or presses Back twice. They see only the viewfinder (or the old diagnosis sheet) with no sign that a job exists - the worker's 'accepted / on the way' updates, Pay and Rate are unreachable unless they think to tap 'Choose from pictures' (which also permanently flips them into Simple mode) or go Find workers -> Request to hit the notice in request.tsx. Likewise the presenter cannot switch the phone from customer to worker from the Lens at all; the only route is via the grid.
confirmed.fix:
The smallest fix is inside `C:\dk\mobile\src\screens\Lens.tsx` and adds no new screens.

1. **Track the open job.** Import `useFocusEffect` from `expo-router` and `openJobId` from `@/lib/requests`. Add the same effect `CustomerHome` uses:
   `const [activeJob, setActiveJob] = useState<string | null>(null);`
   `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { let alive = true; openJobId().then((id) => alive && setActiveJob(id)); return () => { alive = false; }; }, []));`

2. **Show it on the camera.** Inside the `styles.controls` View, above the hint text, render when `activeJob` is set:
   `<Pressable accessibilityRole="button" onPress={() => router.push({ pathname: '/job/[id]', params: { id: activeJob } })} style={styles.linkButton}><Text style={[type.label, { color: colors.worklightAmber }]}>{t('yourActiveJob')} · {t('openJob')}</Text></Pressable>`

3. **Show it on the sheet too.** Pressing Back from the job lands on the Lens while the diagnosis sheet covers the controls. Inside the sheet's ScrollView, above `<DiagnosisSheet>`, render the existing `<Notice title={t('yourActiveJob')} action={t('openJob')} onAction={...push /job/[id]} />` when `activeJob` is set.

4. **Optional, for the presenter.** Render `<ChangeRoleLink />` under the "Choose from pictures" link in the permission-blocked view, or accept the two-tap route through the grid.

One side effect to handle: `LAST_JOB_KEY` is never cleared, and `openJobId()` returns the stored id whenever the network check fails (`requests.ts:139-148`). In the airplane-mode lens demo the pill would appear for a job that was already rated. To avoid that, have `openJobId` call `AsyncStorage.removeItem(LAST_JOB_KEY)` when the online check finds the job missing or no longer open.

confirmed.title: Demo bot abandons a job for good after one failed step, and never resumes jobs already past 'requested' (for example after a bot restart)
confirmed.scenario: serve() adds job.id to `handling` and nothing ever removes it. move() returns false both for a lost race and for a transport error; postgrest-js returns a failed fetch as `error` rather than throwing. On venue Wi-Fi, a single failed request during requested->accepted makes serve() return. The id stays in `handling`, so later sweeps skip the job and the customer's phone shows 'requested' for Ramesh indefinitely. If the failure comes later, or the developer presses Ctrl+C and restarts the bot (for example to add --fast) while a job is 'accepted', 'on_the_way' or 'working', the job is never picked up again. sweep() at line 81 only selects status = 'requested'. A job stuck in 'working' cannot be cancelled by the customer either, because the trigger allows only done or disputed from that state.

confirmed.title: Random 80/20 split puts near-duplicate shots of the same object in both train and validation, so every printed accuracy is inflated
confirmed.scenario: The README and the dataset screen tell the developer to take 3-5 shots of each object. image_dataset_from_directory shuffles all file paths with the seed and takes the last 20% as validation, so almost every validation photo has siblings of the same fan or switchboard in training. Validation accuracy then measures 'same object, another angle' rather than 'a switchboard in a house I have not seen'. Every decision in the script depends on that number: EarlyStopping with restore_best_weights, the per-class report ('if any class is under 0.8, shoot more'), and the int8-versus-fp16 pick. The developer sees about 0.97 everywhere, stops shooting, and the model misfires on the judges' switchboard. The split is also not stratified, so a small class can end up with n=0 validation images and print nan.
confirmed.fix:
Replace `datasets()` in `C:\dk\ml\train.py` with a per-class chronological split built on `tf.data`. `image_dataset_from_directory` cannot take path lists, so it is dropped.

```python
def datasets(root, batch):
    classes = sorted(d.name for d in root.iterdir() if d.is_dir())
    tr, va = [], []
    for i, c in enumerate(classes):
        files = sorted(str(p) for p in (root / c).iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png"})
        cut = int(len(files) * 0.8)            # filenames are Date.now() -> last 20% = objects shot last
        tr += [(f, i) for f in files[:cut]]; va += [(f, i) for f in files[cut:]]
    def load(path, label):
        img = tf.io.decode_image(tf.io.read_file(path), channels=3, expand_animations=False)
        return tf.image.resize(img, (SIZE, SIZE)), label   # same bilinear, non-aspect resize as before, float32 0-255
    def make(pairs, shuffle):
        ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(([p for p, _ in pairs], [l for _, l in pairs]))
        if shuffle: ds = ds.shuffle(len(pairs), seed=SEED, reshuffle_each_iteration=True)
        return ds.map(load, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE).batch(batch)
    return make(tr, True), make(va, False), classes
```

This gives a stratified, almost object-disjoint validation set. At most one boundary object per class leaks. It costs no extra shooting, and the rest of the script (`representative()`, `accuracy()`, the per-class report) works unchanged.

Add one line to README section 1: "shoot each class across at least two locations, and finish each class in a different place than you started, because the last 20% becomes the validation set".

Optionally, also accept a `--val <dir>` argument for photos shot in another house. Load it with `image_dataset_from_directory(val_dir, class_names=classes, shuffle=False, ...)`.

The nan sub-issue needs no fix. It is already handled at line 125, and the stratified split removes it anyway.

confirmed.title: Training stretches 4:3 photos to a square, but the app centre-crops: train/serve preprocessing skew
confirmed.scenario: Dataset mode (takeTrainingPhoto in mobile/src/ai/capture.ts) saves the full upright 4:3 frame, 480x640. train.py loads it with image_dataset_from_directory(image_size=(224,224)). The default is crop_to_aspect_ratio=False, so every training and validation image is squashed to 1:1. Objects end up about 1.33x too wide, with the full field of view. RandomZoom is given only a height factor, so it preserves that distortion. On the phone, takeShot() centre-crops a square (75% of the frame, undistorted) before resizing. A round ceiling fan or a square switch plate is therefore an oval or rectangle in every training image and round or square at inference. The per-class validation accuracy and the int8-vs-fp16 'ship' decision are also measured on stretched images, so they overstate what the phone will do. The developer is about to shoot 1,500 photos and train; they will swap in a model that scores well in the script and does noticeably worse in the airplane-mode snap test, with nothing pointing at the cause.
confirmed.fix:
In `C:\dk\ml\train.py` `datasets()`, add `crop_to_aspect_ratio=True` to the `common` dict:

`common = dict(image_size=(SIZE, SIZE), batch_size=batch, seed=SEED, validation_split=0.2, label_mode="int", crop_to_aspect_ratio=True)`

- The installed Keras supports the argument. It centre-crops each image to a square before resizing, which is the same central `min(width, height)` square that `takeShot` crops on the phone.
- Training, validation, the int8 representative dataset and the `accuracy()` measurement all read from these datasets, so all four are fixed at once.
- No app change is needed, and photos already shot stay usable.
- Optionally add a line to `ml/README.md` and the `dataset.tsx` hint telling the shooter to keep the subject in the middle of the frame, because the top and bottom eighths of each training photo are cropped away.

confirmed.title: 'packet' / 'carton' / 'crate' stamp a confident 'Bulk waste pickup' on any box or snack packet; 'blower' shadows 'hand blower'
confirmed.scenario: A judge holds up whatever is at hand, such as a delivery or cardboard box, a biscuit or chips packet, or a plastic crate. These are high-confidence ImageNet classes ('carton', 'packet', 'crate'). Line 38 maps all three, plus 'plastic bag', to waste/bulk_waste, and scoreCategories sums them. The total easily passes SURE_ABOVE, so the sheet stamps 'Garbage pickup - Bulk waste pickup NN%' with a price and a Find workers button on a photo of a parcel. Separately, rule order makes 'blower' (line 16) match the label "hand blower" before the generic appliance rule on line 18. The 'hand blower' and 'hair dryer' keywords there are dead, and a hair dryer is routed to 'Fan not working'.
confirmed.fix:
In `C:\dk\mobile\src\ai\labelMap.ts` line 16, remove 'blower' from the fan rule:

`[['electric fan'], { category: 'appliance', problem: 'fan_dead' }],`

- "electric fan" and the full-synset label "electric fan, blower" both still match 'electric fan', so the existing check on `ai-test.ts` line 16 keeps passing.
- "hand blower" then falls through to the generic appliance rule on line 18 and opens the appliance sub-problem list.
- Optionally add one check: `hitForLabel('hand blower')` returns category 'appliance' with problem undefined.

The waste rule on line 38 needs no mandatory change. It is a judgment call for the user's planned label-map tuning:

confirmed.title: 'sure' verdict ignores unmapped / 'other' probability mass, so the phone can stamp a category when its top answer was 'not a job'
confirmed.scenario: scoreCategories drops every label with no Hit, including the fine-tuned 'dikhado:other' class. diagnose() then compares only the surviving sum with SURE_ABOVE = 0.45. After the fine-tuned model is swapped in, a wall photo can score other=0.53 and electrical/switchboard=0.46. The sheet shows 'Looks like: Switch or socket 46%' and speaks the safety card, although the model's own top class was 'other', the class added precisely so the phone can say it cannot tell. With the stock model, a laptop on a table can score 'laptop' 0.5 (unmapped) against desk + folding chair + dining table = 0.46, which is stamped as Carpentry. The cause is that 0.45 is below 0.5, so a 'sure' category need not be the majority.
confirmed.fix:
Keep `SURE_ABOVE` at 0.45 and compare the best category against the single strongest unmapped label, not against 1 minus the mapped sum.

- In `diagnose()` (C:\dk\mobile\src\ai\diagnose.ts), after `classify`, compute `topUnmapped`: the maximum of `probabilities[i]` over every `i` where `hitForLabel(labels[i] ?? '')` is null. `hitForLabel` needs importing from './labelMap'. For the fine-tuned model this value is simply P('dikhado:other').
- Change line 32 to `if (scores[0].confidence >= SURE_ABOVE && scores[0].confidence >= topUnmapped) return { kind: 'sure', ... }`. Anything else falls through to the existing 'unsure' branch, which still shows the tile under "Is it this?".
- Add one case to C:\dk\mobile\scripts\ai-test.ts: labels ['dikhado:other', 'dikhado:electrical/switchboard'] with probabilities [0.53, 0.46] should give kind 'unsure'.
- Stock-model results change only when one unmapped label outscores a category whose summed confidence is 0.45 or more, which is rare.

confirmed.title: 'Book another' after a finished job returns to the old diagnosis sheet, camera off, instead of a fresh lens
confirmed.scenario: Lens stays mounted under /workers -> /request -> /job with stage='sheet', shot and diagnosis intact (that is correct for a plain Back from /workers: the sheet is still there, camera inactive, Retake works). But job/[id].tsx:125 ends the happy path with router.dismissTo('/home'). On the exact demo path (snap -> Find workers -> request -> bot drives to done -> pay -> rate -> 'Book another') the judge lands on the previous photo's paper sheet: 'Looks like: <old category> NN%', old thumbnail, dark status bar, safety advice not re-spoken, viewfinder off (isActive is false because stage is still 'sheet'). To start the next booking they have to scroll to the bottom of the sheet and find the small 'Retake' link. Nothing is broken, but the app appears stuck on the last job rather than ready for a new one.
confirmed.fix:
**Smallest fix: two edits, no new module.**

1. In `C:\dk\mobile\src\app\job\[id].tsx:125`, change the action to `onAction={() => router.dismissTo({ pathname: '/home', params: { fresh: String(Date.now()) } })}`. POP_TO reuses the existing home route and only replaces its params (`StackRouter.js:379-400`), so Home does not remount but sees a new param.

2. In `C:\dk\mobile\src\screens\Lens.tsx`, import `useLocalSearchParams` from expo-router and `useEffect` from react. Then add:
   - `const { fresh } = useLocalSearchParams<{ fresh?: string }>();`
   - `useEffect(() => { if (fresh) retake(); }, [fresh]);`

   `fresh` is undefined on first mount, so nothing happens then. A plain Back from `/workers` does not change the param, so the sheet with the other guesses is kept.

3. Optional hardening: move `tuck.value = 0` from `retake()` to the first line of `snap()`, after the `stage !== 'camera'` guard. The frame and sheet views are unmounted by the `setShot(null)` and `setDiagnosis(null)` state change, so the old photo is not blown up to full screen for a frame during the pop transition. `tuck` is still 0 well before `takeShot` resolves and the new frame mounts.

An alternative with no params is a module-level `pendingReset` flag, set by 'Book another' and consumed in a Lens effect keyed on `focused`.

confirmed.title: Training squashes 4:3 photos to 224x224, but the app centre-crops to a square before resizing
confirmed.scenario: Dataset mode saves the full 4:3 frame (640x480 or 480x640, from takeTrainingPhoto). image_dataset_from_directory(image_size=(224,224)) uses crop_to_aspect_ratio=False by default, so every training and validation image is stretched by 1.33x on one axis and shows the whole frame. At inference, Lens -> takeShot() centre-crops the same HD_4_3 photo to a square and then resizes, so there is no distortion and the field of view is narrower. RandomZoom is given only a height factor, so it preserves aspect and no augmentation covers the gap. The validation and TFLite accuracy printed by the script are measured on squashed images too, so the mismatch does not show up in any number. The developer ships a model that scores well in train.py and is noticeably less confident on the phone. Round objects such as fans, and taps near the edge of the frame, are affected most.
confirmed.fix:
In `C:\dk\ml\train.py` line 40, add `crop_to_aspect_ratio=True` to the `common` dict:

`common = dict(image_size=(SIZE, SIZE), batch_size=batch, seed=SEED, validation_split=0.2, label_mode="int", crop_to_aspect_ratio=True)`

Keras then centre-crops the largest square before resizing, which is the same geometry as `takeShot` in `capture.ts`. Training, validation, INT8 calibration and the TFLite accuracy check all read these datasets, so the one flag covers all four. `requirements.txt` pins TF 2.15-2.16, and both support the flag.

Leave `takeTrainingPhoto` and `dataset.tsx` alone. Saving the full frame is correct, and no reshoot is needed.

Optional: narrow `RandomZoom` to about `(-0.15, 0.1)`, so zoom-in on top of the crop does not make training framing consistently tighter than the phone's.

confirmed.title: No way to remove a photo shot under the wrong class chip, and the pull script restores laptop-side deletions
confirmed.scenario: While walking a house, the developer switches between the fan, switchboard and tap chips in a horizontally scrolling row. Across about 1,500 shots, some will land under the previous chip, for example ten tap photos saved into electrical__switchboard. The screen has no undo or delete, so the only fix is to delete the files on the laptop. ml/pull_dataset.sh is documented as 'safe to re-run as you shoot more', and it re-extracts every file from the phone. The mislabelled photos return on the next pull and end up in training. One stray photo under a class that was never meant to be shot also creates a one-image class, which train.py gives a class_weight of about total/(n_classes*1).
confirmed.fix:
**1. "Undo last" button in `C:\dk\mobile\src\app\dataset.tsx`**
- In `shoot()`, build the destination once: `const dest = new File(dir, `${Date.now()}.jpg`)`.
- Move the temp file to `dest`, then store `{ file: dest, cls }` in a `useState` or ref named `last`.
- Add a small "Undo last" Pressable beside the shutter, shown only when `last` is set.
- On press:
  - `try { last.file.delete() } catch {}`
  - `setCounts(c => ({ ...c, [last.cls]: Math.max(0, (c[last.cls] ?? 1) - 1) }))`
  - `setLast(null)`
- Decrement `last.cls`, not the currently selected `cls`. The developer has usually switched chips by the time they notice the mistake.

**2. Docs**
- Add one line to `C:\dk\ml\README.md` section 2, and the same note to the header comment of `pull_dataset.sh`. Suggested wording: "A re-pull restores anything you deleted only on the laptop. Delete bad shots on the phone with Undo, or with `adb shell run-as in.dikhado.app rm files/dataset/<class>/<file>`, or do your laptop-side clean-up after the final pull."

**3. What not to change**
- Do not make the pull script mirror-delete `ml/dataset/`. If the phone's app data is ever cleared, that would destroy the only remaining copy of the photos.

confirmed.title: pull_dataset.sh preflight reports the wrong problem when two devices are attached or a non-debuggable build is installed
confirmed.scenario: (1) With the second phone plugged in for the open Phase 2 two-phone check, or with an emulator running, `adb get-state` exits non-zero with 'more than one device/emulator'. Its stderr goes to /dev/null and the script prints 'No phone found. Connect it over USB...', so the developer ends up replugging cables. (2) If the release APK has been installed over the debug build for a rehearsal, `run-as` fails with 'package not debuggable'. Line 10 treats any failure as a missing directory and prints 'No dataset on the phone yet... shoot some photos first'. The photos are still in files/dataset, and Dataset mode does not exist in that build, so it reads as if two hours of shooting were lost.
confirmed.fix:
Replace lines 9-10 of `C:\dk\ml\pull_dataset.sh` with versions that surface adb's own error and branch on it. Both forms are safe under `set -euo pipefail`.

```bash
if ! err=$(adb get-state 2>&1); then
  echo "adb: $err"
  case "$err" in
    *"more than one"*)
      adb devices
      echo "Two devices attached. Run: ANDROID_SERIAL=<id above> bash ml/pull_dataset.sh" ;;
    *)
      echo "No phone found. Connect it over USB and allow USB debugging." ;;
  esac
  exit 1
fi

if ! err=$(adb shell run-as "$APP" test -d files/dataset 2>&1); then
  case "$err" in
    *"not debuggable"*|*"unknown package"*|*"is unknown"*)
      echo "The installed DikhaDo is not the debug build, so adb cannot read its files. Your photos are still on the phone. Reinstall the debug build (same signing key, so data is kept) and run this again." ;;
    *)
      echo "No dataset on the phone yet. Open DikhaDo > Dataset mode and shoot some photos first." ;;
  esac
  exit 1
fi
```

`adb` honours `ANDROID_SERIAL` for every later command in the script, so nothing else needs to change. Optionally add one line to `C:\dk\ml\README.md` about `ANDROID_SERIAL` when two phones are attached.

confirmed.title: Confidence % is the summed CATEGORY probability but it is printed next to (and routes on) a SUB-PROBLEM chosen from one label
confirmed.scenario: labelMap.scoreCategories adds every matching label into the category (confidence += p) while `problem` comes from the single strongest label (labelMap.ts:81-91). diagnose() applies SURE_ABOVE (0.45) to the sum, and the sheet then stamps bestEntry = byCode(problem) with Math.round(best.confidence*100)% beside it and sends 'Find workers' straight to /workers/<problem>. Example with the stock model on a desert cooler or mixer: electric fan 0.20, space heater 0.15, loudspeaker 0.12, radio 0.10 -> appliance = 0.57 -> kind 'sure' -> stamp reads 'Fan not working  57%' and the button skips the sub-problem list (where 'Cooler or fridge repair' lives) and lists fan workers. The phone's real evidence for a fan was 20%, below its own 'sure' bar. Same for switch 0.2 + table lamp 0.15 + spotlight 0.12 -> 'Switch or socket 47%'. A judge reads '57%' as confidence in the words on the stamp; it is not. This will also skew the label-map tuning the user is about to do from on-phone results. (The bare 'NN ms' is classify() only, which is honest as inference time; no change needed there.)
confirmed.fix:
Make the fix in `C:\dk\mobile\src\ai\labelMap.ts` `scoreCategories` only. Track each sub-problem's own probability and drop `problem` when it does not dominate its category.

1. Give each category entry a `Map<string, number>` called `problemMass`. For every hit that has a `problem`, add `p` to `problemMass[hit.problem]`.
2. When building the `CategoryScore`, take the largest `problemMass` entry. Keep `problem` only if its mass is at least 0.6 × `entry.confidence`. Otherwise return `problem: undefined`.

Use the 60% share, not an absolute `SURE_ABOVE` on the sub-problem. With an absolute bar, a verified fan shot such as electric fan 0.35 plus 0.12 of other appliance labels would stop routing straight to fan workers. With the share rule it still does.

No change is needed in `DiagnosisSheet.tsx`, `destinationFor` or `diagnose.ts`. With `problem` undefined:
- The stamp reads "Fan and appliances 57%".
- "Find workers" routes to `/category/appliance`, where "Cooler or fridge repair" is listed.
- Unsure-state tiles behave the same way.

Optional change for strict honesty: add `problemConfidence` to `CategoryScore`, and have the sheet show that number instead of the category sum whenever a problem is kept.

Add two cases to `C:\dk\mobile\scripts\ai-test.ts`:
- fan 0.20, space heater 0.15, loudspeaker 0.12, radio 0.10 → category `appliance`, `problem` undefined, `destinationFor` screen `category`.
- fan 0.40, washer 0.10 → `problem` `fan_dead` kept.

confirmed.title: The diagnosis stamp - the one word the screen exists to show - is amber text on form paper at 2.55:1 contrast
confirmed.scenario: Stamp text uses color worklightAmber #C77A16 on formPaper #D9E2DE with a 2px amber outline. Relative luminances 0.261 vs 0.744 give a contrast ratio of 2.55:1; 18px medium is not 'large text', so the floor is 4.5:1 (3:1 even for large). Everywhere else amber is used as a fill under lensInk text or as an icon on a dark well; this is the first amber-on-paper text in the app. Scenario: rural user outdoors at a pump or tractor in daylight on a budget LCD, or the judge looking at a projected/mirrored phone: 'Bike and tractor repair' / 'బైక్, ట్రాక్టర్ రిపేర్' is the faintest thing on the sheet, fainter than the muted 'This looks like' caption above it (onPaperMuted is ~7:1). Thin Telugu/Devanagari strokes at 2.55:1 wash out first.
confirmed.fix:
Make two one-line changes in `C:\dk\mobile\src\components\DiagnosisSheet.tsx`.

1. On line 85, change the stamp text colour from `colors.worklightAmber` to `colors.onPaper`.

   - I would not use the amber-fill, `lensInk`-text variant. Its contrast is fine at 5.7:1, but it would look like a second tappable button directly above the amber "Find workers" `PrimaryButton`.

2. On line 131, add `flexShrink: 1` to `styles.stamp`. A long name at a large system font size then wraps inside the stamp instead of pushing the percentage off the right edge of `stampRow`.
